newsitem.title: ITALY: Number up for Italian tax evaders.
newsitem.headline: Number up for Italian tax evaders.

text.p: Italians can now rat on tax dodgers at the touch of a telephone pad.

A new three-digit freephone number, similar to those for police, ambulance and fire services, has been introduced by finance police in Italy, where taxes are high and fiscal evasion is almost a national sport.
A finance police official said the "117" service was drawing a heavy response, with people reporting shops for not giving them proper receipts and unregistered door-to-door salesmen.
The emergency service got a cool reception from the Italian artisans' guild on Tuesday.

"The number will only help catch small-time crooks knocking off the state for a handful of lire," the association said in a statement. "Ninety percent of fiscal fraud is invisible to the most sophisticated radar," it added.
The new number allows people to make anonymous accusations. Some newspaper commentators said it could mostly be used by spurned lovers or people looking to settle family feuds.
